answer: For a route-planning market, publish tasks identifying a haven, a ledge or a summit on a fixed map. Each task has an escrowed fee and a unique ID; a verifier checks a submitted route against the map, pays the first valid result, then marks that ID spent. There is no signup subsidy or per-account minimum payout. Extra aliases cannot replay the same route for more fees. An attacker must solve additional funded tasks and win their races, paying computation per new reward rather than profiting from extra keys.
